stories.headline: Sources: Steelers to trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
stories.summary: The Steelers have agreed to trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
After a lengthy and contentious contract standoff and a lingering back issue, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is going to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Steelers on Wednesday night agreed to trade Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources told ESPN.

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined by a back injury.

The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle.

Porter, who started 41 games and had three interceptions in three seasons, missed all of the team's training camp and preseason after reporting an aggravation to the back injury during the team's mobility workout on the first day of camp. He was placed on the physically unable to perform list until roster cutdown day in late August.

Porter was then a limited participant in every regular-season practice until earlier this week as coach Mike McCarthy said the cornerback was progressing through a "ramp-up" phase during the first month of the season.

Porter was inactive for each of the first three games and had been ruled out of the Steelers' Thursday night game against the Browns in Cleveland earlier Wednesday. The Steelers added a back injury to Wednesday's practice report in addition to the "not injury related-conditioning" description the team used for Porter's injury status for most of the past three weeks. Porter had previously been a full participant in the team's Monday and Tuesday walkthroughs.

His departure means the Steelers will continue to operate with Asante Samuel Jr., Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette rotating at outside cornerback. Everette, a 2026 third-round draft pick, played extended snaps in the Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals, first coming in for a briefly injured Dean and then replacing Samuel for much of the second half.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones hinted back in training camp that he would be willing to give up draft capital to help this season's team. Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday about a potential trade with reports of the team's interest in Porter.

While not specifically talking about Porter because of tampering rules, Jones said, "I'd just say we're right on top of it. We're very aware of the moving parts out here."

The Cowboys have had a need for cornerback help with Cobie Durant expected to miss his second game because of a hamstring strain. In last week's loss to the Baltimore Ravens, Durant's replacement, Shavon Revel, injured his knee and ankle. He was limited in Wednesday's practice. Revel missed the first eight games of his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL in his right knee sustained while at East Carolina, but the current injury is to his left knee.

At the end of the game against the Ravens, the Cowboys used backups Caelen Carson and Ameer Speed opposite DaRon Bland with Reddy Steward, a practice squad call-up, working the slot.

This is the third trade between the Cowboys and Steelers in the past two years. In May 2025, the Cowboys sent a 2026 third-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder to Pittsburgh for wide receiver George Pickens and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

In August, the Cowboys acquired tackle Broderick Jones and a 2027 fourth-rounder for third- and sixth-round picks in 2027.

The Ringer first reported news of the Porter trade.

stories.headline: Gavin Sheets' pinch-hit homer propels dominant Padres past Cubs 4-1 for 2-game Wild Card sweep
stories.summary: — Pinch-hitter Gavin Sheets blasted a two-run homer, five Padres pitchers combined on a five-hitter, and San Diego swept the Chicago Cubs out of the NL Wild Card Series with a 4-1 victory in Game 2 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- — Pinch-hitter Gavin Sheets blasted a two-run homer, five Padres pitchers combined on a five-hitter, and San Diego swept the Chicago Cubs out of the NL Wild Card Series with a 4-1 victory in Game 2 on Wednesday night.


Xander Bogaerts drove in the first run for the surging Padres, who followed up their 8-0 victory in Tuesday's opener with another dominant mound performance. The Cubs led the majors in runs and the NL in homers this year, but they managed just eight hits — seven singles — over 18 innings against San Diego's inspired staff.


Ethan Salas drove in a run while becoming the youngest player to catch a postseason game in major league history for the Padres, whose 20-3 surge since Sept. 5 has them looking like a threat in the NL.


One year after the Cubs eliminated the Padres in three tough Wild Card games at Wrigley Field, the Padres reversed the result in two romps before frenzied sellout crowds at Petco Park.


With their fifth playoff series victory in the past seven years, the Padres advanced to face the MLB-best Milwaukee Brewers in an NL division series this weekend.


Nico Hoerner had half of the Cubs’ hits in the series, and he drove in Chicago’s only run in the fourth inning. He also got their only extra-base hit of the series with a ninth-inning double off Mason Miller, but the Padres’ vaunted closer calmly finished the save and set off another massive celebration on the field.


Probable NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong and veteran slugger Alex Bregman struggled mightily atop the Cubs’ lineup in San Diego, going a combined 0 for 15 with a walk and eight strikeouts over these two games. Bregman played just over a week after he was hit in the face with a foul ball.


After hitting two homers in the first inning of Game 1, the Padres waited until the second inning of Game 2 to take a 2-0 lead. Ty France led off with a double off Kevin Gausman and scored on Bogaerts’ single before Salas hit a line-drive flyout to center, scoring Jackson Merrill.


Salas, the prized 20-year-old prospect recalled Sept. 1, also became the youngest player to appear in a postseason game for the Padres.


Chicago finally scored when Seiya Suzuki singled and eventually came home on Hoerner’s ground ball to center off starter Nick Pivetta. Rookie manager Craig Stammen immediately yanked Pivetta in favor of his intimidating bullpen, and Bradgley Rodríguez escaped a bases-loaded jam.


Rodríguez also pitched the fifth to earn the victory in his postseason debut.


After Bogaerts’ double chased Gausman in the fourth, Sheets blasted a 100.8 mph fastball from Daniel Palencia into the right-field bleachers. Sheets, the fan-favorite outfielder who is playing with a nagging plantar injury in his left foot, delivered his second career postseason homer and his first since 2021 as a White Sox rookie.


The shot was the Padres’ first pinch-hit postseason homer since 2005, and their long-suffering fans’ cheers rattled the park.


Up next
Game 1 of the division series is Saturday in Milwaukee. The Padres took four of six from the Brewers this season, even sweeping a three-game series at Petco Park in August.

stories.headline: Wings' Ogunbowale scores record 45 to force Game 3 vs. Valkyries
stories.summary: Arike Ogunbowale delivered a record-breaking performance with the Wings' season on the line, scoring 45 points, including a tying 3-pointer to force overtime, to help Dallas force a deciding Game 3 against the Valkyries.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Arike Ogunbowale scored a WNBA playoff-record 45 points, including a tying 3-pointer in the final seconds of regulation, and the Dallas Wings beat the Golden State Valkyries 108-100 in an overtime thriller Wednesday night, forcing a deciding Game 3 in their first-round series.

Ogunbowale opened the extra period by banking in a 3, then hit another one to put Dallas ahead for good at 103-100 with 1:46 left. She easily topped her previous playoff best of 24 points.

The four-time All-Star's off-balance corner 3 for a 93-93 tie with 4.1 seconds left in Game 2 was followed by Gabby Williams getting called for an offensive foul on the inbounds play after a Golden State timeout.

That call was reversed on replay, so instead of Aziaha James having a chance to give Dallas the lead at the free throw line, there was a jump ball at center court with 3.0 seconds to go. After a scramble for the loose ball, Golden State's desperation shot was way off target, and after the buzzer.

The deciding game will be Friday night in San Francisco, where the Valkyries won the series opener by 24 points. Golden State is looking to advance in the playoffs for the first time in the franchise's second season.

The late drama overshadowed an off night for Wings star Paige Bueckers, who is making her postseason debut. The 2025 No. 1 pick and Rookie of the Year scored 10 points on 3-of-13 shooting.

Williams scored a career-high 36 points, regular season or playoffs, but missed all six of her shots in the final 1:31 of overtime to finish 12-of-23 from the field.

Dallas' Alysha Clark tied her playoff career high with 21 points and James added 13.

Kaila Charles scored 14 points for the Valkyries, and Kayla Thornton had 13. Cecilia Zandalasini was limited to three shots and five points after leading Golden State with 22 in the series opener.

With the scored tied at 98 in the extra period, Ogunbowale and Tiffany Hayes had to be separated after making contact. Both were called for flagrant fouls, and each made a pair of free throws with 2:26 left.

The Valkyries didn't score again, shooting 2-of-12 in overtime.

stories.headline: Triple premiership-winning coach Chris Fagan steps down at Brisbane
stories.summary: Brisbane's triple premiership-winning coach Chris Fagan has coached his last game at the club.
stories.body:
Brisbane's triple premiership-winning coach Chris Fagan has coached his last game at the club, despite still having a year to run on his contract.

Fagan, who coached the Lions to a third successive flag last Saturday, made the call to step down from his role after 10 years of service. The 65-year-old announced his decision to the playing group on Thursday ahead of the club's best and fairest night.

Taking over senior coaching duties at Brisbane in 2017, Fagan led the club for 243 games and 148 wins, including the last three premierships. He walks away as one of just six men in history to coach a three-peat.

Football manager Danny Daly, who left a career in banking to join Collingwood in 2000 before stints at North Melbourne and Richmond, and assistant coach Cameron Bruce are among the top early candidates to take over.

Fagan has also heaped praise on backline coach Dale Morris, who suggested the idea of using "Wharfie Time" to motivate the Lions if the Dockers reached for the button in the Grand Final.

More to follow...

stories.headline: Maple Leafs beat the Islanders 2-1 to rebound from opening loss
stories.summary: — Easton Cowan had a goal and an assist in the first period and the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the New York Islanders 2-1 on Wednesday night for their first victory under coach Jim Hiller.
stories.body:
TORONTO -- — Easton Cowan had a goal and an assist in the first period and the Toronto Maple Leafs beat the New York Islanders 2-1 on Wednesday night for their first victory under coach Jim Hiller.


The Maple Leafs rebounded from a 3-2 home loss to Montreal in their opener Tuesday night, spoiling the Islanders' first game of the season.


Colton Sissons also scored for Toronto, and Anthony Stolarz made 26 saves.


Emil Heineman scored in the third period for New York. Ilya Sorokin stopped 24 shots.


Sissons redirected his first goal for Toronto at 7:14 of the first period off Nick Paul's setup. Cowan then shoveled home a power-play rebound with 8:05 left in the period.


Reunited with fellow netminder Sergei Bobrovsky after winning the Stanley Cup together with Florida in 2024, Stolarz was perfect until Heineman scored short-handed with 5:51 left.

stories.headline: St. Louis up to 2nd place with unbeaten run now at 17 games
stories.summary: Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
Simon Becher and Tomas Ostrak each scored late in the second half as St. Louis City SC beat the New York Red Bulls 3-0 on Wednesday night.

St. Louis (13-6-8) extended its unbeaten streak to 17 matches in MLS play and moved up to second place in MLS' Western Conference table.

New York (9-12-6) entered having conceded just two goals in its last four games, with Ethan Horvath recording three shutouts.

The Red Bulls had won their last two games, but were without rising stars Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall for the game, with the pair away on national team duty for the United States.

Rafael Navarro opened the scoring just five minutes into the game when he redirected Conrad Wallem's header across the goal.

Becher capitalized on a New York turnover deep in its own half to make it 2-0 in the 87th minute. Ostrak sent in a rebound in stoppage time.

Roman Bürki made four saves to earn his third clean sheet of the season for St. Louis.

It was the first time New York and St. Louis have met during the regular season.

St. Louis hosts the LA Galaxy next on Oct. 11, while the Red Bulls play San Diego FC at home the day before.

stories.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
stories.summary: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs him to do right now."

Brown was the last player on the court after practice, working on handling double teams in the post - by kicking out to a shooter or fading away for a jumper along the baseline - with a massive Sixers logo on the wall of the practice facility behind him.

Maxey made sure to acknowledge the transition for Brown, too, as he begins life with the Sixers after having played for the Boston Celtics for his entire career before being traded within the Atlantic Division in July.

"This is very foreign to him, imagine being somewhere for [10] years and coming here, the team that you're trained to hate, probably," Maxey said. "It's been great. Especially [since] we just beat [Boston in the playoffs]. It's kind of crazy."

stories.headline: Ayrton Senna's Honda NSX could fetch £800,000 at London auction
stories.summary: A 1991 Honda NSX that once belonged to Ayrton Senna will go up for auction in London at the end of October.
stories.body:
A 1991 Honda NSX that once belonged to Ayrton Senna will go up for auction in London at the end of October.

Chassis number T000233 was one of three NSXs delivered to Senna as part of his contract with Honda in the early 1990s and, due to its provenance, carries an estimate of £500,000 to £800,000.

When the car first went on sale in 1990 it had a list price of between £52,000 and £55,000, with low-mileage NSXs from the same era currently listed online for up to £135,000.

The legendary Japanese sports car is closely linked to Senna, who contributed to its development before it went on sale as Honda's answer to the more expensive Porsche and Ferrari sportscars of the era.

Chassis T000233 is finished in Formula Red over a black leather interior and was delivered to Portugal in March 1991 so that Senna could make use of it while staying at his property in Quinta do Lago.

According to the listing on Sotheby's website, the NSX featured in the 1992 documentary, 'Ayrton Senna: Racing Is In My Blood' and was used by the Brazilian to commute to the 1991 Portuguese Grand Prix in Estoril.

Senna, who died in an accident at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, won all three of his world titles with Honda power while racing at McLaren.

stories.headline: Roosters star admits he is torn on World Cup decision
stories.summary: Robert Toia has revealed he is still undecided if he wants to play for Australia or Tonga in the World Cup, less than a week out from teams being named.
stories.body:
Robert Toia has admitted he still doesn't know who he wants to play for at the World Cup, as the in-demand centre weighs up representing Tonga or Australia.

Toia is the highest-profile player caught in a tug-of-war between nations, with the World Cup just a fortnight ago and final squads to be announced next week.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf had told AAP this week that Toia had indicated he wanted to represent the Pacific nation, after debuting for them last year.

Australia counterpart Kevin Walters has also made clear he believes the Sydney Roosters star is available for the Kangaroos, and he has not been told otherwise.

Toia has accepted he must make a decision soon, but remains uncertain what way he will go with Sunday's NRL grand final against Newcastle before this month's tournament.

"To be honest, I have not made my mind up," Toia told AAP.

"I just find it hard that I don't have a decision. I want to play for Tonga, it means so much to my family, myself and my people.

"I went over to Tonga last year and you can see how much it means to them.

"But to have Australia on your resume. Just to play for Australia, in my second year, I find it such a massive achievement. That's what I'm kind of weighing up."

Beyond Toia, Woolf also believes Sydney Roosters teammates Salesi Foketi and Siua Wong want to play for Tonga in the global showpiece.

Queensland winger Jojo Fifita revealed this week he too was still undecided, weighing up whether to play for Australia, New Zealand or Tonga.

Fifita told AAP he'd had discussions with all three nations, although he was not named in the Kiwis' initial 40-man squad.

Walters has said both Jojo and his brother David are under consideration for Australia's World Cup squad.

In better news for Tonga, Dolphins halfback Isaiya Katoa has confirmed he will be fit for the tournament after a syndesmosis injury in the preliminary-final loss to the Roosters.

"I don't need surgery. I will be able to play in the World Cup," Katoa said.

"I immediately knew I had done something, so I was definitely happy once I got the scans back it wasn't too bad and I will be able to represent Tonga."

Complicating matters for players who are weighing up their future is the fact Australian representatives stand to earn $40,000 by playing in the tournament.

AAP is aware of coaches and players who are concerned that may prompt some players to choose the Kangaroos in order to benefit their families.

But Katoa said it would never be a factor for him.

"I'd never look at the price tag, it's always where my heart is at," he said.

"I've always said my heart is at Tonga and if it wasn't for Tonga I am half-Cook Islands as well. So if it wasn't for Tonga, I would go Cook Islands."

Meanwhile it is understood Tonga will pick former St George Illawarra half Talatau Amone in their squad for the tournament.

Amone has not played since he was deregistered by the NRL in 2023 for assault. Tonga are still yet to learn if he will be cleared to play in the tournament.

He can return to the NRL next year, and starred on his return to Queensland Cup with Wynnum-Manly in recent months.

stories.headline: 2026 MLB playoffs: Offseason questions for eliminated teams
stories.summary: Here's how the winter looks in Chicago, Boston and Houston after they were swept out of the playoffs.
stories.body:
October never even started for the Chicago Cubs, Boston Red Sox and Houston Astros.

With a trio of wild-card sweeps Wednesday, they became the first teams to make exits in the 2026 MLB playoffs -- on the last day of September.

So, what's next for Chicago, Boston and Houston -- and all of the other teams that won't be celebrating a World Series parade this fall? For every eliminated contender this October, ESPN MLB experts Jorge Castillo, Bradford Doolittle, Alden Gonzalez, Jesse Rogers and David Schoenfield list its key free agents and biggest offseason questions and also make their predictions for the long, cold winter ahead.

Teams eliminated in wild-card series

Chicago Cubs
Eliminated by: San Diego Padres

Key free agents: RHP Kevin Gausman, OF Ian Happ, OF Seiya Suzuki, LHP Shota Imanaga, LHP Matthew Boyd (mutual option), RHP Clay Holmes (player option), C Carson Kelly (mutual option)

Biggest offseason priority: The Cubs need to rebuild their pitching staff and that includes both their rotation and bullpen. The good news is they can concentrate on that part of their team because they have enough position players to fill the void left by Happ and Suzuki, who are both likely to leave the team via free agency. But what does that staff look like with Justin Steele and eventually Cade Horton returning from injury? Do Holmes and Boyd return? One but not the other? And what to make of a bullpen which was inconsistent? It's a yearly debate under Jed Hoyer, who doesn't like to spend big money on closers. The Cubs have paid for that decision at times -- though in other moments they've developed some good relievers. Pitching is the key to their offseason, whether it comes from within or from outside the organization.

What will they do at catcher? Veteran Carson Kelly has been nothing short of excellent over his two years in Chicago. He's great at calling a game. He's great at the ABS challenge system. And he's been more than a serviceable hitter. Plus, he's a leader and a glue guy in the clubhouse. Chicago has an up-and-coming catcher in Owen Ayers and still has Miguel Amaya under team control, while Kelly has a mutual option, so it'll be interesting how the team handles that position.

Offseason prediction: The Cubs will likely do what they usually do: Spend some on their rotation, but not on the pen. They shelled out a few dollars for middle guys in Phil Maton and Hunter Harvey last year and it didn't work out, so unless they have an appetite for a big-time closer -- they almost never do -- it feels like they'll try to build their bullpen with minor additions and under-the-radar guys. Boyd might return, but Holmes, Imanaga and Gausman will test the market, opening up some slots in the rotation. -- Rogers

Boston Red Sox
Eliminated by: New York Yankees

Key free agents: RHP Sonny Gray ($30 million mutual option), LHP Patrick Sandoval, IF Isiah Kiner-Falefa

Biggest offseason priority: Gray had a terrific season but has hinted at retirement, telling The Boston Globe that he would retire "in a heartbeat" if his family wants him home, so replacing him in the rotation could be the priority. A healthy Garrett Crochet will help fill that void, but after trading away so many starting pitchers and pitching prospects over the past year (including Kyle Harrison, Shane Drohan, Hunter Dobbins, Connelly Early, Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon), adding depth in that department looks necessary.

Will they trade Jarren Duran? While the Red Sox had a revolving door at shortstop and second base in 2026 -- six different players started at short and seven at second -- those positions will probably be resolved in 2027 with top prospect Franklin Arias and Curtis Mead, the trade deadline acquisition the Red Sox were going to play at second base until he got injured his first game with the team. Trevor Story still has one more year left on his contract, but there's no reason he should be playing ahead of Arias next season.

That leaves trading Duran on the agenda. Roman Anthony's nearly four-month stint on the IL meant the four-outfielders-for-three-positions problem never actually turned into a problem, but after hitting just .207/.266/.361, Duran is clearly fourth on the depth chart. His trade value took a nosedive, but he still somehow has two years left of team control, and the Red Sox will find a team willing to take a chance on him.

Offseason prediction: Even if there was no looming lockout, it would project as a quiet offseason for the Red Sox. The trades for Willson Contreras last offseason and then Mead, Adley Rutschman and reliever Erik Miller at the deadline brought in players with control through at least 2027. Maybe Duran gets traded, maybe it's time to give up on Tristan Casas ever getting healthy. If Gray returns -- $30 million is certainly a reason to stick around -- the Red Sox are in outstanding shape to return to the playoffs and make a run at the AL East title. -- Schoenfield

Houston Astros
Eliminated by: Chicago White Sox

Key free agents: RHP Bryan Abreu, 3B Isaac Paredes (club option, converted to mutual option if Paredes lands in top 10 of AL MVP balloting)

Biggest offseason priority: The Astros navigated the stretch run without a general manager after Dana Brown was let go in late August. That was after the draft and the trade deadline, so the committee guiding the front office was able to make it work. Going forward, the Astros will need to find or promote a new lead executive, then empower him to implement his own processes. Given the influence of owner Jim Crane and ex-player Jeff Bagwell, a vocal analytics skeptic in the past, the outcome of the search will tell us a lot about how the higher-ups in Houston see the landscape of best practices in the industry. That can be good, or not, but either way it's time the Astros returned some continuity to their most important baseball operations position.

How much weight should the Astros put on this playoff appearance? Of course the Astros deserved to celebrate the latest in the spree of division titles the franchise has won over the past decade. And it's certainly true that Houston's ability to climb out of a 20-31 hole in late May was fairly remarkable. Nevertheless, the Astros had to win their last two games to reach .500 at season's end and were outscored by 32 runs overall. If not for the low bar the AL West set this season, the Astros would have been watching from the playoff sideline for a second straight season. Thus, as the next Astros GM sets out, they'll have to be clear-eyed about it. The starting point for the club is one of mediocrity and there aren't enough upward-pointing trajectory arrows on the roster. Maybe a full reset isn't needed, but at the very least, the short and the long terms will have to be given equal shrift, or else this thing could really crumble in a hurry.

Offseason prediction: Houston has had a coterie of bright front office personalities working out of the spotlight going back to the Jeff Luhnow days. The most obvious course of action would be to promote one of them -- someone like assistant GMs Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey or Connor Huff. But just as crucial is to empower that hire to build and run their own front office. Questions about whether the Crane/Bagwell-led leadership team is willing to fully commit to that are why a promotion from within seems like the most likely course of action. The first indication about how this will go probably will be whether the Astros wait to have a new baseball chief in place before committing to bringing back manager Joe Espada in 2027. -- Doolittle

stories.headline: Former draftee slams AFL over concussion plight
stories.summary: An AFL draftee whose life was upended by a concussion injury says he "was so close to ending everything".
stories.body:
An AFL draftee whose life was upended by a concussion injury says he "was so close to ending everything".

Aiden O'Driscoll, who had to retire because of a devastating training injury without making his AFL debut, also slammed the league as an "absolute joke".

"The last couple of years I've experienced nothing but pain, and I've explained it multiple times to you. You're supposed to help AFL players through hardship, not leave them with absolutely nothing," O'Driscoll wrote in his extensive Instagram post.

His comments came a day after Geelong announced defender Jake Kolodjashnij had retired.

Last month, the Cats were fined $140,000 and current AFL chairman Craig Drummond apologised after it emerged the club had agreed to a secret concussion waiver with Kolodjashnij. Drummond was Geelong president at the time the agreement was struck.

The Geelong controversy highlighted the complexity and sensitivity around contact sport's concussion crisis.

The Western Bulldogs recruited O'Driscoll in the 2023 draft. But a head injury that summer left him with significant ongoing health problems and the club announced in May, 2024 that he had retired on medical grounds.

"The doctors described my concussion as 'one of the worst' they've seen, with eight micro brain bleeds, and (a) fracture behind my ear," O'Driscoll wrote.

"From a medical point of view, losing my career, my identity plus going through the symptoms I have, you'd think the AFL would be useful with some support?

O'Driscoll added it took the AFL six weeks to find him a psychologist.

"Through this period, I was grieving the most, it got to the point where I started questioning my life? If it was worth living?," he wrote.

"I was so close to ending everything, I would've been free from all the pain/trauma. My family/close friends and partners honestly kept me here."

Melbourne premiership player Angus Brayshaw also had to retire in 2024 because of his concussion issues.

In his emotional toast to other retiring players at the Brownlow Medal function that year, Brayshaw referred to O'Driscoll by name.

"I know a few other past players that are dealing with the same issues as I am," O'Driscoll said.

"AFL it's time to step up! I'm a 21-year-old that can't keep suffering each week. While you're at it, help the other past players that need support."

O'Driscoll added he had been told at 18 never to play contact sport again.

The AFL and the players' association were contacted for comment.

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

stories.headline: Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City
stories.summary: Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would "wait and see" before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.
stories.body:
Jürgen Klopp said Wednesday he would wait to see how things pan out before commenting on the Premier League's announcement yesterday that Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges for breaching financial rules.

The charges cover a period between 2009 and 2018, with Klopp's tenure at Liverpool -- which began in 2015 -- overlapping with the time that City were have found to be guilty of breaking Premier League rules.

On the eve of Germany's match against Serbia in the Nations League, though, Klopp seemed content to let his record at Merseyside speak for itself instead of speculating over what might have been.

"I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course," Klopp said. "Should any sanctions be imposed, I naturally have nothing to do with it anyway, and that's why I'm waiting to see how things pan out. But when you're talking about legal proceedings that have been going on for so long now, I assume there will be an appeal or something like that? That will take ages again of course.

"So I'm a long way from preparing myself for it in any way and I don't have any feelings about it."

City, who won the Premier League three times between 2009 and 2018, have denied all of the charges and are set to lodge an appeal against the verdict.

Of his longtime rival and Man City coach Pep Guardiola, Klopp said: "I also know what I said about it in the past and how if there's ever a parade, I'll be there. But it doesn't feel like that anymore. My respect for Pep Guardiola and the football played at City during the time we played against each other, in the way they played back then and how they brought football to life on the pitch -- plus what an opponent they proved to be for us at the very highest level -- is far too great for me to be able to say anything now."

Klopp was also tight-lipped on Germany's captain for the Nations League tie -- his third match in charge of the national team. The new Germany coach has a completely new squad to work with after he selected two groups for the four fixtures during this international window.

With regular captain Joshua Kimmich allowed to leave the camp after he featured in a 1-1 draw in the Netherlands and the shock home loss to Greece, Klopp must decide who wears the armband for this clash in Munich.

"The team will be led onto the pitch tomorrow by the player with the most international caps," Klopp said on Wednesday.

Captain question aside, Klopp did hint that Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig would play at his home stadium of Allianz Arena.

"Feel free to ask 'who might be a captaincy option,' but I don't reveal the starting lineup now. You can look them up yourselves," said Klopp. "I can only say that Jonas Urbig won't wear the armband in his first international match."

Urbig took part in a news conference after Klopp and expressed his delight at making his Germany debut.

"It's a moment you've worked towards your whole life and I'm simply delighted to have the opportunity tomorrow to play here in our own stadium and do my part to help us as a team achieve our first victory," Urbig said. "This No. 1 topic isn't something I'm concerned with. My focus is really on reaching my limit every day and pushing it even further. And everything else will perhaps fall into place over time."

Germany are without a win in four fixtures after a World Cup last-32 exit to Paraguay followed a group-stage loss to Ecuador, but Serbia are on an equally poor run.

Serbia have lost both Nations League fixtures by a 2-1 score to the Netherlands and Greece, respectively, after they suffered heavy defeats to Cape Verde and Mexico during the summer.

"Serbia's approach won't be much different from what Greece did. What makes Serbia particularly difficult to play against is their experience," Klopp said. "They also have some excellent footballers. They know all the tricks of the trade, so we have to be prepared for that.

"It's not the best period in Serbian football at the moment, but the players themselves know what's at stake. An opponent that sits deep is a major challenge for any team, at any stage of development."

Following the game against Serbia on Thursday, Germany will close out Nations League play for the September/October international window with a second match against Greece, this time in Thessaloniki on Oct. 4.

stories.headline: NBA preseason buzz: Latest on trades, news and intel
stories.summary: The NBA regular season is less than a month away, and we're tracking all the news, deals, and trades across the league.
stories.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season officially kicked off Sept. 22 as the Houston Rockets held their media day, before the Dallas Mavericks followed suit Friday.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 30

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost.

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin

Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special

Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp.

Goodwill on the latest between the Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns: "It wasn't so much what he said, like this full-throated defense of himself, but he said, 'I would like to get my contract done.'

"He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up.

"And then someone else, I think Ian Begley asked him, 'Are you OK with playing this out through the season or do you want to table contract talks?' and he basically said, 'Everybody's going to be a little uncomfortable around here.'"

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
